current.kana: こんげつのなのかわすいようびだ

structure_explanation.en: A classic identification structure 'A は B だ' (A is B). The target is the vocabulary of dates. 今月の七日 ('the 7th of this month') uses の to link 今月 (this month) to 七日 (the 7th); this expression becomes the topic with は, and 水曜日 (Wednesday) is the predicate, closed by だ (the casual form of 'to be').
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Estrutura clássica de identificação 'A は B だ' (A é B). O alvo é o vocabulário de datas. 今月の七日 ('o dia 7 deste mês') usa の para ligar 今月 (este mês) a 七日 (dia 7); essa expressão vira o tópico com は, e 水曜日 (quarta-feira) é o predicado, fechado por だ (forma casual de 'ser').

translation_literal.en: As for the 7th of this month, it is Wednesday.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto ao dia 7 deste mês, é quarta-feira.

translation.en: The 7th of this month is a Wednesday.
translation.pt-BR: O dia 7 deste mês é quarta-feira.

gloss.en: day (of the month); counter for days

role.en: counter suffix (forms 七日 = なのか, 'the 7th')
role.pt-BR: sufixo contador (forma 七日 = なのか, 'dia 7')

note.en: だ = casual/affirmative form of the copula

objections.objection: To make kana/romaji come out なのか the patch assigns r="なの" to the token ７ (gloss 'seven (numeral)') while 日 keeps r="か". ７ is never read なの; なのか is an indivisible whole-word reading of 七日. Sentence-level kana/romaji are now correct, but per-token furigana would render なの over ７ and か over 日, i.e. the critical wrong token reading (なな) is replaced by a different wrong token reading rather than removed. The op names the clean alternative.
objections.auditor_hint: merge tokens[4]+[5] into a single token ７日 with r="なのか" instead of slicing the reading across the numeral and the counter

current.jp: 雨が降っているけれども出かけます
current.kana: あめがふっているけれどもでかけます

structure_explanation.en: The target is けれども ('but'). Note that here it joins a VERB in the 〜ている form (降っている = 'it is raining'), not an adjective. The connection is correct: common form of the verb + けれども. The second part 出かけます ('I will go out', polite form) contrasts with the rain. (It would be wrong to write 降っているだから; with a verb the correct option is 〜から or, for contrast, けれども.)
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O alvo é けれども ('mas'). Repare que aqui ele se liga a um VERBO na forma 〜ている (降っている = 'está chovendo'), e não a um adjetivo. A conexão é correta: forma comum do verbo + けれども. A segunda parte 出かけます ('vou sair', forma polida) contrasta com a chuva. (Seria errado escrever 降っているだから; com verbo o correto é 〜から ou, para contraste, けれども.)

translation_literal.en: It's raining, but I'm going out.
translation_literal.pt-BR: A chuva (sujeito) está caindo, mas/contudo (eu) saio.

translation.en: It's raining, but I'm going out.
translation.pt-BR: Está chovendo, mas eu vou sair.

note.en: て-form of 降る (降っ + て), base of the progressive 〜ている
note.pt-BR: forma て de 降る (降っ + て), base do progressivo 〜ている

note.en: いる forming 〜ている: ongoing action ('it is raining')
note.pt-BR: いる formando 〜ている: ação em andamento ('está chovendo')

note.en: stem (連用形) of 出かける, before ます
note.pt-BR: radical (連用形) de 出かける, antes de ます

objections.objection: The whitespace op rewrote this token array but left two phantom tokens at the head: tokens[0] 出/で and tokens[1] かけ/かけ, an alternative segmentation of 出かけ that also appears in full at tokens[9]. Concatenating the after tokens yields 出かけ雨が降っているけれども出かけます and でかけあめがふっているけれどもでかけます, which do not match the after jp or kana. Shipping this leaves the token array describing a different string than the sentence it belongs to, which is the same class of corruption the op was opened to remove.
objections.auditor_hint: Delete tokens[0] and tokens[1] and reindex; the array should start at 雨/あめ.

current.jp: 弟が電気を消しました
current.kana: おとうとがでんきをけしました

structure_explanation.en: The target is the transitive/intransitive pair. 消す is the TRANSITIVE verb (to turn off/put out something): someone performs the action, so the light takes を and the agent (弟) takes が. Compare with the intransitive 消える ('to go out by itself'). 消しました is the polite past.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O alvo é o par transitivo/intransitivo. 消す é o verbo TRANSITIVO (apagar/desligar algo): alguém faz a ação, então a luz leva を e o agente (弟) leva が. Compare com o intransitivo 消える ('apagar-se sozinho'). 消しました é o passado educado.

translation_literal.en: As for my younger brother, he turned off the light.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto ao irmão mais novo, a luz, apagou.

translation.en: My younger brother turned off the light.
translation.pt-BR: Meu irmão mais novo apagou a luz.

gloss.en: to turn off, to switch off (something)

note.en: stem of 消す in ます form
note.pt-BR: raiz de 消す em forma ます

note.en: ます in the past: まし + た
note.pt-BR: ます no passado: まし + た

objections.objection: The literal mirrors present 弟が as a topic: "As for my younger brother" / "Quanto ao irmão mais novo". There is no は in 弟が電気を消しました - が is the subject marker, and the item's whole pedagogical point is the transitive frame agent-が / object-を. The As-for / Quanto a device must mirror は only, so this teaches the wrong particle function in the very sentence whose explanation was just tightened.
objections.auditor_hint: en: "My younger brother (subject), the light, turned off." / pt-BR: "O irmão mais novo (sujeito), a luz, apagou."

current.jp: テーブルの上にコップが四つあります
current.kana: てーぶるのうえにこっぷがよっつあります

structure_explanation.en: The sentence uses the existence pattern [place に + subject が + あります]. テーブルの上 (the top of the table) is the place, joined by の and に; が marks コップ as what exists; 四つ is the quantity (four units); and あります is the existence verb for inanimate things. Note that the number 四つ stands free before the verb, with no particle, as is common with quantifiers.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase usa o padrão de existência [local に + sujeito が + あります]. テーブルの上 (a parte de cima da mesa) é o local, ligado por の e に; が marca コップ como o que existe; 四つ é a quantidade (quatro unidades); e あります é o verbo de existência para coisas inanimadas. Note que o número 四つ vem solto antes do verbo, sem partícula, como é comum com quantificadores.

translation_literal.en: On top of the table, glasses, four (of them), there are.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Em cima da mesa, copo(s) quatro(-unidades) existe(m).

translation.en: There are four glasses on the table.
translation.pt-BR: Tem quatro copos em cima da mesa.

note.en: 四つ (yotsu) = four units, native counter つ
note.pt-BR: 四つ (yotsu) = quatro unidades, contador nativo つ

note.en: あり stem of ある (existence of things); here linked to ます
note.pt-BR: raiz あり de ある (existência de coisas); aqui ligada a ます

note.en: ます in the present; あります = polite form of ある
note.pt-BR: ます no presente; あります = forma polida de ある

objections.objection: The critical op for tokens[6].r explicitly states "The attached note on the つ token also romanizes it 'yotsu' instead of 'yottsu'", and that half of the op was not applied. kana/romaji were corrected to よっつ / yottsu and token 四 to よっ, but both notes still read "四つ (yotsu) = four units" / "四つ (yotsu) = quatro unidades". The record now teaches the corrected reading in the transcription and the wrong one in the gloss note sitting directly under it.
objections.auditor_hint: en: "四つ (yottsu) = four units, native counter つ" / pt-BR: "四つ (yottsu) = quatro unidades, contador nativo つ"

current.kana: かみにながいせんをひいた

structure_explanation.en: The particle に marks 紙 ('paper') as the surface where the line ends up (target/place of result) — unlike で, which marks where an action occurs. 長い ('long') is an i-adjective that modifies 線 ('line'), and を marks that line as the direct object of the verb 引く ('to pull/draw'), here in the past 引いた. The vocabulary focus is 線.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A partícula に marca 紙 ('papel') como a superfície onde a linha fica (alvo/local do resultado) — diferente de で, que marca onde a ação ocorre. 長い ('comprida') é um adjetivo い que modifica 線 ('linha'), e を marca essa linha como objeto direto do verbo 引く ('puxar/traçar'), aqui no passado 引いた. O foco de vocabulário é 線.

translation_literal.en: On the paper, I drew a long line.

translation.en: I drew a long line on the paper.
translation.pt-BR: Desenhei uma linha comprida no papel.

note.en: い-adjective 長い in the present, modifying 線
note.pt-BR: adjetivo い 長い no presente, modificando 線

note.en: stem of 引く used with the auxiliary た (引いた, past)
note.pt-BR: raiz de 引く usada com o auxiliar た (引いた, passado)

note.en: auxiliary た: past form of 引く
note.pt-BR: auxiliar た: forma passada de 引く

objections.objection: The rewrite newly introduces em dashes into learner-facing text in both locales ("(target/place of result) — unlike で" and "(alvo/local do resultado) — diferente de で"). These are the only em dashes in the whole batch and they did not exist in "before"; the batch convention is comma/parenthesis punctuation.
objections.auditor_hint: en: "...as the surface where the line ends up (target/place of result), unlike で, which marks where an action occurs." / pt-BR: "...como a superfície onde a linha fica (alvo/local do resultado), diferente de で, que marca onde a ação ocorre."
